## ResourceDescriptor.id property

Contract of the resource's identifier: it encodes and decodes the `id` of every identity reference to this resource, including references that appear as another reference's container.

**Signature:**

```typescript
readonly id?: ValueType<Id>;
```

## Remarks

Absent when the resource has no identifier. Such a resource can be referenced only by selector forms (name, index, every, or range); an identity reference to it is rejected when encoding and decoding.

When the identifier is matched on a property of the object (`byProperty`<!-- -->), such as its name, resolving an identity reference has the meaning of a selector on that property: it resolves to whatever object has that value when it is resolved, and when several share it, to the first match in the app's order. Such a reference does not pin one particular object unless the value is claimed unique.

When the identifier is a key the app's collection finds the object by (`byKey`<!-- -->), the app interprets the key: a key that names a location, such as a path, resolves to whatever object is at that location when it is resolved.
